name: Holy Roman Empire
claim: Translatio imperii: Charlemagne crowned "Emperor of the Romans" by Leo III (800); Otto I (962). Neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire — Voltaire.
end: Francis II abdicates and dissolves the Empire, 6 August 1806

name: Latin Empire of Constantinople
claim: Crusader regime installed in the capital after the sack of 1204; recognised by almost nobody east of Venice.
end: Michael VIII Palaiologos retakes Constantinople, 25 July 1261

name: Empire of Trebizond
claim: Komnenian splinter state on the Black Sea whose rulers styled themselves "Emperor and Autocrat of all the East".

name: Ottoman Empire (Kayser-i Rûm)
claim: Mehmed II adopted "Caesar of Rome" after 1453; the sultans held Constantinople — and the claim — for 469 years.

name: Palaiologos heirs
claim: Andreas Palaiologos sold his title to Charles VIII of France (1494), then willed it to Ferdinand and Isabella (1502). Nobody has used it since.
end: Claim bequeathed to the Spanish crown and never exercised

name: Tsardom / Empire of Russia (Third Rome)
claim: "Two Romes have fallen, the third stands, and a fourth there shall not be" (Philotheus of Pskov, c. 1510). "Tsar" derives from Caesar.

name: First French Empire
claim: Eagle standards, a Senate, a "King of Rome" for an heir (1811), and an emperor crowned in a laurel wreath. Strong aesthetic claim.
end: Waterloo, 18 June 1815; second abdication four days later

name: German Empire (Kaiser)
claim: "Kaiser" is Caesar with a German accent; the Hohenzollerns inherited the Holy Roman vocabulary, not the territory.

name: Fascist Italy (Terza Roma)
claim: Mussolini's "Third Rome" rhetoric, fasces on everything, and an "Emperor of Ethiopia" (1936). Rome was the capital, which helped the branding.
end: Mussolini dismissed, 25 July 1943; Italian Republic from 1946

name: The Papacy (Holy See)
claim: Holds the title Pontifex Maximus, the Latin language, and the postcode. Has never claimed the Empire — merely outlived it.
end: Ongoing. Not a claim; a tenancy.
